claims.text: Conventional metallic rollers and guide plates undergo rapid chemical corrosion when directly exposed to high-temperature molten aluminum.
Conventional metallic rollers and guide plates undergo erosion when directly exposed to high-temperature molten aluminum.
Chemical vapor deposition or another advanced deposition technique can produce a uniform, adherent hexagonal BN coating on the equipment parts.
A continuous hexagonal BN coating acts as a physical barrier between the metallic substrate and molten aluminum.
Hexagonal BN is chemically inert toward high-temperature molten aluminum.
Hexagonal BN is non-wetting with respect to molten aluminum.
Hexagonal BN has sufficient high-temperature stability for hot dip aluminum plating conditions.
Hexagonal BN has low surface energy.
Hexagonal BN's low surface energy minimizes wetting by molten aluminum.
The BN coating minimizes chemical interaction between molten aluminum and the coated surface.
Preventing direct contact between molten aluminum and the substrate reduces corrosion.
Preventing direct contact between molten aluminum and the substrate reduces erosion.
BN-coated components will lose less mass than uncoated components under identical hot dipping conditions.
BN-coated components will exhibit less surface degradation than uncoated components under identical hot dipping conditions.
BN coating will produce a statistically significant extension of component service life relative to uncoated parts.
The protective effect depends on the BN coating remaining intact and adherent during continuous high-temperature exposure and thermal cycling.
Coating delamination or thermal fatigue can compromise the protective efficacy of the BN layer.
The magnitude of service-life extension and corrosion reduction depends on coating quality, coating thickness, and thermal-cycling conditions.
